blocks.en: D.1 Latency
blocks.zh: D.1 延迟

blocks.en: Table 21 gives two delays from the test client. The wait runs from the client’s end-of-audio signal to the service’s last message, so it excludes endpointing. That last message is the final text for Meta, Gemini, ElevenLabs, GPT-Live and RT Whisper, the end-of-session message for AAI and Zoom, the closed connection for Deepgram, and an end-of-audio message for our own deployments; for the session-message cases the wait can run slightly past the last text. The connect time is how long a session takes to open. The median (p50) and a slow case (p90) are given, with up to six sessions at a time per system. The AAI models have the slowest p90 (over 1,200 ms). Only Gemini’s wait grows with clip length (591 ms under 20 seconds, 1,084 ms over a minute). Repeat runs moved waits by up to 320 ms, so treat them as indicative.
blocks.zh: 表21列出了测试客户端的两次延误。 等待从客户端的终端信号到服务端的最后一个消息,因此排除了端点. 最后一条信息是Meta、双子座、11Labs、GPT-Live和RT Whisper的最后文本、AAI和Zoom的结束会话信息、Deepgram的关闭连接,以及我们自己部署的结束会话信息;对于会话信息案例,等待可以略过最后的文本。 连接时间是会话开放需要多长时间. 给出了中位数(p50)和一个慢例(p90),每个系统每次最多6场. AAI模型拥有最慢的p90(超过1200 ms). 只有双子座的等待时间长得短(591米不到20秒,1 084米超过一分钟). 重复运行移动等待最多320毫秒,所以把它们当作指示.

blocks.en: Table 21: Delays over all single-language sessions. Wait: from the end of the audio to the final text. Connect: from opening the connection to the session being ready. p50: median; p90: 90% of sessions were faster.
blocks.zh: 表21:所有单一语文课的延误情况。 等等:从音频结尾到最终文本. 连接:从打开连接到会话准备. p50:中位数;p90:90%的会话更快.

blocks.en: A timing run on the 106 English messages recorded when text was first finalised and the round trip to each provider (Table 22 ). Whisper SH, Qwen, Deepgram, Zoom and AAI finalise text during speech on 83–99% of messages, typically 5–9 seconds in; Meta, Gemini, GPT-Live and RT Whisper finalise only at the end, as set up. ElevenLabs finalised the first 36 seconds early on every message longer than about 35 seconds. Subtracting the round trip moves Deepgram from seventh to third, but the same six rows stay slowest, at 594–716 ms beyond it.
blocks.zh: 第一次最后确定文本时记录的106条英文信息的时间和前往每个提供者的往返时间(表22)。 Whisper SH, Quen, Deepgram, Zoom 和 AAI 在83–99 % 消息的演讲中最终完成文本, 通常为 5–9 秒; Meta, 双子座, GPT-Live 和 RT Whisper 最终仅按设定在结尾. 11Labs在每条超过35秒的信息上提前完成了前36秒. 减掉回程将Deepgram从第7位移到第3位,但相同的6排保持最慢的速度,在594–716ms的距离之外.

blocks.en: Table 22: Timing run on the 106 English messages. Final text during speech: share of messages with finalised text before the audio ended. First final text: median time from the start of the audio to the first finalised text, over those messages. Round trip: median TCP handshake time to the provider during the runs, about 300 samples each; for services behind a content-delivery network (OpenAI, Zoom, and in part Gemini and Meta) it reaches only the nearest edge server, so it understates the round trip to the model.

blocks.en: Clean recordings score 2.1–4.6%. A far microphone in quiet adds under 3 points for Whisper SH, Gemini, the AAI models and ElevenLabs, 4–6 for Meta, Deepgram, GPT-Live, RT Whisper and Zoom, and 8–10 for Qwen and gated Whisper. blocks.en: With its VAD off, the gated deployment drops 5 or more words from the last third of 44% of whispered clips, and the self-hosted deployment has no cut-off endings; on EARS they miss 30.5% and 10.4% of whispered words (Table 27 ). The gated server’s own speech detection, which was not measured, may account for part of the difference. Cutting at pauses is as fast: 361 against 360 ms typical, 498 against 596 ms slow case.

blocks.en: The two stock phrases (Finding 4) give the self-hosted deployment 19.5% WER on Spanish (Spain), twice the gated setup’s 10.0%. blocks.en: 1. Gated, VAD on (“gated Whisper”). A deployment on Baseten with a voice gate on the client: a Silero VAD in front of Whisper drops audio it judges to be silence: it waits for speech above a 0.5 probability, keeps 96 ms before it, sends at most 512 ms of any pause, and stops sending after 544 ms of silence. The deployment cuts the audio into segments itself, with its own server-side speech detection, which is not under our control. 2. Gated, VAD off. The same deployment, sent all of the audio: the client’s Silero VAD is off, but the server’s own speech detection still runs. 3. Self-hosted, Silero cuts (“Whisper SH”). A second deployment of our own, which does no segmentation. The client runs the same VAD only to decide where each segment ends: at a pause of 544 ms after speech, once at least 5 seconds have been sent, and always before 30 seconds. It then tells the server to transcribe that segment. Every sample of audio is sent. 4. Self-hosted, Silero drops. The same deployment, with Silero VAD also dropping audio as in setup 1. 5. Self-hosted, TEN cuts. Setup 3 with TEN VAD [ 54 ] , an open VAD from the TEN framework, in place of Silero, at its default threshold of 0.5. Every sample is sent. 6. Self-hosted, TEN drops. Setup 4 with TEN VAD: the same rules decide which audio is dropped, using TEN’s speech probabilities instead of Silero’s. 7. OpenAI GPT-Realtime-Whisper (“RT Whisper”). OpenAI’s hosted streaming Whisper. 8. OpenAI Whisper-1. OpenAI’s file transcription, so the whole recording is uploaded when the user stops. 9. Whisper-1 split. Whisper-1 with the client cutting the recording at pauses, using the VAD rule of setup 3, and uploading each segment as soon as it is cut, with the previous segment’s text as context. A segment in which the VAD heard no speech is not sent.

blocks.en: TEN does not keep whispered speech by calling everything speech: on fan noise, steady noise, mains hum and television it calls about as much audio speech as Silero, and at most 2.2% of the windows of any no-speech clip. It does call much more background talk speech: with babble, 97% of windows against 80% for Silero, 15 points more than on the same recordings without babble; what Whisper writes when TEN passes that audio was not tested. On EARS, TEN also beats Silero when only cutting (9.5% against 11.5%, difference 95% CI − 3.7 -3.7 to − 0.3 -0.3 ), because it calls more whispered audio speech; on no-speech clips both call almost none (0.4% and 0%). Dropping with TEN gives the self-hosted deployment 7.2% on quiet English (8.3% sending all audio, within its interval), 17.6% averaged over other languages, 14.7% on Spanish (Spain) instead of 19.5%, and text on 2 no-speech clips instead of 6. The cost is a slightly longer wait (395 against 361 ms) and more lost languages (54% against 45% with English, 96% against 87% without).
blocks.zh: TEN不通过调用一切语音来保持低声讲话:在风扇噪声,稳态噪声,主哼声和电视上,它调用和Silero一样多的音频演讲,最多还有2.2%的无声片段窗口. 它确实叫来更多的背景演讲:用booble,97%的窗口对Silero的80%,比没有booble的同一录音多15分;Whisper在TEN通过时写道,音频没有经过测试. 在EARS上,TEN还击败了Silero只剪接(9.5%对11.5%,差幅95% CI − 3.7-3.7对0.3-0.3),因为它呼唤更多的低声音频讲话;在无声片段上,几乎不打(0.4%和0%)。 使用TEN的投放使自备部署在静音英语上达到7.2%(8.3%在它的间隔内发送所有音频),其他语言平均为17.6%,西班牙语(西班牙)为14.7%,而不是19.5%,无话语片段为2个,而不是6个。 成本是稍长的等待时间(395比361毫秒)和较多的失落语言(54%比45%为英语,96%比87%为无英语)。

blocks.en: Both dropping setups were repeated at thresholds 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 on the whispered, fan-on and no-speech clips (Figure 2 ). Silero’s whispered WER falls only from 51.4% to 41.1%, because even at 0.2 it calls 52% of whispered audio speech; TEN stays at 10.0–10.7%. Fan-on WER moves by at most 2.1 points, and no-speech clips with text stay at 0 of 10 for Silero and 2 of 10 for TEN.
